title: Record Number of People Injured by Nara Deer
paragraphs: Japan's ancient city of Nara is popular with tourists for its many shrines, temples and gardens. But Nara has something else that's rather unusual — a large park where deer and humans mix freely.

Deer have lived with humans in Nara for over 1,300 years, so they're quite used to us! The Nara deer are believed to be sacred messengers of the Shinto gods, so they're protected. A common activity for tourists is feeding the deer special rice crackers called shika senbei, and the deer will approach people hoping for these treats.
However, it's important to remember that even though these deer are used to humans, they're still wild animals. And sometimes the deer can be a little aggressive when people forget that they're wild.

In fact, according to Nara City Hospital, the number of people who have had to go to hospital after being injured by deer in Nara has been increasing over the last five years — and this year, it already reached a record high of 51 people by November 5.
The increase in injuries is said to be because of increases in the number of deer — and also increases in the number of visitors to Nara.
This year, the Nara Deer Preservation Foundation counted 1,687 deer in Nara — a record high, and an increase of 222 from last year.
Experts warn that some tourists may have the wrong idea about the animals, thinking they're friendly and can be petted. But people can be knocked over by the deer or hurt by their antlers.

The website of the Nara Deer Preservation Foundation suggests that people do not approach the deer or touch them, and if people have rice crackers for the deer, they should give them to the deer quickly and not tease the animals. Elderly people and people with small children should be especially careful around the deer.
